display.title: Episode 149: Dama ben Nesina's Diamond, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi starts a phone-in Mitzvah Time contest on honoring parents, a young yeshiva student leads the Shema, and the Gemara's story of Dama ben Nesina and his diamond begins.
display.summary_long: After the Hakochainik march and a cheese commercial from the sponsor, Uncle Yossi announces a brand-new contest: each week he will teach a mitzvah, then telephone a listener who sent in a postcard and ask a question about it, with a Tzivos Hashem prize for a correct answer. The first mitzvah is kibbud av va'em, honoring father and mother, which Hashem placed in the Ten Commandments and rewards with long life. A young yeshiva student visiting Studio 604 leads everyone in the first twelve words of the Shema. Story time brings a story from the Gemara: Dama ben Nesina, a kind farmer who honors his father, finds a huge diamond in his field. His father locks it in a box and keeps the only key under his pillow. Messengers of the Kohen Gadol arrive ready to pay any price, but when Dama comes back from the house he stands before them silent and grave, and the chapter ends there. The show closes with the new Moshiach Times, a short listener's letter from Uncle Yossi's mailbox, birthday requests and Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Honoring your father and mother is so important that Hashem put it in the Ten Commandments and promised long life as its reward.
